html: The vessel wall under noise is not only oxidised, it is infiltrated, and the two are the same story told twice: most of the oxidase that does the damage arrives inside cells that were not there before. This module draws the endothelial side of that arrival. The oxidant made next door is the signal: micromolar hydrogen peroxide frees the transcription factor NF-kB from its inhibitor, which is held in the cytoplasm until the kinase phosphorylates it and it is degraded. The freed dimer enters the nucleus and is read at two genes whose promoters carry its binding sites. One is VCAM1, whose message rises in the aorta of noise-exposed mice and falls again when the myeloid cells are taken away; its protein reaches the luminal surface, where a flowing leucocyte is caught by the integrin VLA-4, first tethered, then rolling, then arrested. The other is IL6, and plasma interleukin-6 rises from the second day of exposure. The module ends where the arrested cell sits on the endothelium, because what that cell brings with it is the oxidase of the entry module: ablating these cells leaves the noise-exposed vessel with its endothelial function, its blood pressure and its redox state almost intact, while the brain's inflammation gets worse. The glyph for the adherent cell is therefore the point of the map, and the single most useful thing it says is that the vascular damage of noise is in large part delivered rather than generated.
